meanings.note: Interrogative or exclamative word before verbs or nouns.
Conjunction or relative pronoun linking two clauses.

examples.trans: They say that it is true.

meanings.note: Adjective meaning out of the ordinary (che straordinario odore).
Used as a masculine plural noun in the workplace for overtime.
Neutral word for any scent or odour, pleasant or unpleasant.

examples.trans: What a wonderful smell of coffee!

meanings.note: Marks possession, material, department (stagista di regia), or topic.
Links verbs like dire, chiedere, pensare to a following infinitive.
Invariable English borrowing universally used in Italian production.

examples.trans: There is no smoking on set.

meanings.note: Unstressed 1st-person singular direct, indirect, or reflexive pronoun (mi sento, mi piace, mi serve).
Imperative senti grabs a listener's attention ('listen / look').
Mi sento a casa ('I feel at home'); sentirsela (te la senti?, 'do you feel up to it?').

examples.trans: Listen, do you have a minute?

meanings.note: Marks destination, location in cities, or indirect recipient.
Links activities and idioms such as giocare a tennis or a presto.
Often used without an article after a and da: a casa, da casa.

examples.trans: I will call you from home.

meanings.note: Before a past participle, marks something that happened moments ago.
Before a clause, introduces an immediate trigger.

examples.trans: I will call you as soon as I can.

meanings.en: can; may; to be able to
meanings.note: Modal verb expressing ability or permission.

mollare.gloss: to quit; to drop; to let go of

meanings.en: to quit; to give up on
meanings.note: Lively informal verb for walking away from a job, project, or habit.

Invariable feminine noun.

stare.gloss: to stay; to be; to live

meanings.note: Stai fermo ('stay still'), stare in porta ('play in goal').
Come stai?, sto scherzando (stare + gerund for ongoing action), sta a Milano ('lives in Milan').

examples.trans: I am writing a note right now.

meanings.note: Sto scherzando means 'I am just kidding'.

examples.trans: I am not joking, I mean it.

meanings.note: Location or state; in silenzio means quietly, in porta means in goal.
Truncates to gran before many nouns (in gran forma); un grande means 'a legend'.

examples.trans: He works in a big studio.

meanings.note: Essere / stare in gran forma means being on top form.

examples.trans: Today I am in top form!

meanings.note: Informal greeting.
Informal farewell.
Question word asking manner or requesting repetition (Come, scusa?).
Introduces a comparison.
Adverbial counterpart of buono; in va bene it expresses agreement.
Standard expression of gratitude in all registers.
Identity, description, location, and passive/intransitive auxiliary; with ci forms c'è ('there is').
Movement away from the speaker or toward a destination.
Used in expressions like va bene, ti va, or andare male.
Links to game and sport names with preposition a: giocare a tennis, a biliardino.
Invariable masculine sport noun; giocare a tennis ('to play tennis').
Before a plural noun (certe volte), means 'some / certain'.
Used alone as an emphatic affirmative reply.

examples.trans: Of course, I am coming right away!

meanings.note: Origin in space or time (da casa, da oggi, da capo).
Before a person's name (vai da Duccio), means going to where they are.

examples.trans: I am going over to Arianna's.

meanings.note: Written work or legal agreement; da contratto means under one's contract.
Familiar singular subject pronoun; darsi del tu means addressing each other informally.
Standard negative particle placed immediately before the verb (plus any clitics).
Unstressed familiar 2nd-person singular direct, indirect, or reflexive pronoun.
Modal verb followed directly by an infinitive.

examples.trans: I have to talk to you.

meanings.note: Parlare con means speaking with someone; parlare male di means criticising.

examples.trans: I need to talk to you.

meanings.note: Pushes a conversation or task to a later time.

examples.trans: We will talk about it later.

meanings.note: Coordinating conjunction introducing contrast or surprise (ma guarda!, ma come?).

examples.trans: I wanted to come, but I am working.

meanings.note: Takes a direct object without 'at'; guarda! draws someone's attention.

examples.trans: I have to watch the equipment.

meanings.note: Invariable interrogative pronoun referring to people.
First-person singular subject pronoun; usually included for contrast or emphasis.
Default masculine singular definite article before most consonants.
Before the noun often means 'another / newly arrived' (il nuovo stagista); after the noun, 'brand-new / unfamiliar' (un luogo nuovo).

examples.trans: I am looking for a new place.

meanings.note: The singular spelling is the same for a man or woman; the article and plural distinguish them.
Both the craft of directing and the directing department on a film crew.
Negative reply; in se no ('if not'), means 'otherwise'.

examples.trans: Run, otherwise you will be late.

meanings.note: Da oggi in poi means 'from today onwards'.

examples.text: Da oggi in poi cambia tutto.

meanings.note: Sequences actions (e poi..., poi ti racconto); da oggi in poi means 'from today onwards'.

examples.trans: First we work, then we eat.
Later I will explain everything to you.

meanings.note: Contact someone by voice or telephone.
With mi/ti/si, expresses someone's or something's name.
The thing liked is the grammatical subject (ti piace Seppia?, ti è piaciuta la fotografia?).
Standard polite farewell suitable with both acquaintances and strangers.
